title: Multilingual Hallucination Gaps in Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2410.18270v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as alternatives to traditional search engines given their capacity to generate text that resembles human language. However, this shift is concerning, as LLMs often generate hallucinations, misleading or false information that appears highly credible. In this study, we explore the phenomenon of hallucinations across multiple languages in freeform text generation, focusing on what we call multilingual hallucination gaps. These gaps reflect differences in the frequency of hallucinated answers depending on the prompt and language used. translated_title: 大型语言模型中的多语言幻觉差距
translated_abstract: 随着大型语言模型（LLMs）生成类人文本的能力不断增强，它们正日益被用作传统搜索引擎的替代品。然而，这种转变令人担忧，因为LLMs经常产生幻觉，即那些看似高度可信但实则具有误导性或虚假的信息。在本研究中，我们探讨了自由文本生成中跨多种语言的幻觉现象，重点关注我们所谓的“多语言幻觉差距”。这些差距反映了幻觉答案出现的频率因提示词和所用语言的不同而存在差异。为了量化这类幻觉，我们使用了FactScore指标，并将其框架扩展到了多语言环境中。我们使用来自LLaMA、Qwen和Aya系列的大型语言模型进行了实验，生成了19种语言的人物传记，并将结果与Wikipedia页面进行了比较。我们的结果揭示了幻觉率的显著变化，尤其是在高资源语言和低资源语言之间。
tldr: 该研究提出了“多语言幻觉差距”这一新概念，通过将FactScore指标扩展至多语言环境，并在19种语言上进行传记生成实验，揭示了大型语言模型的幻觉率因语言不同而存在显著差异，尤其是高资源语言与低资源语言之间。
en_tdlr: This study introduces the novel concept of "multilingual hallucination gaps" and, by extending the FactScore metric to a multilingual setting with biography generation experiments across 19 languages, reveals significant variations in LLM hallucination rates depending on the language used.
